record.original_question: Sketch-and-solve: Let (A R^n x d ) be a full-rank matrix, (B R^n x p ) be a matrix, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $d$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let (~ X = (Omega^ -> p A)^+(Omega^ -> p B) R^d x p ) be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution $X = A^+B$. (Here, $^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A ~ X - B |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) _X R^d x p |AX - B |_ F? ]

evidence.quote: Let \(A \in \mathbb R^{n \times d}\) be a full-rank matrix, \(B\in\mathbb R^{n \times p}\) be a matrix, and let \(\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n \times k}\) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $d$ and injectivity \(1-\varepsilon\). Let \(\tilde X = (\Omega^\top A)^+(\Omega^\top B) \in \mathbb R^{d \times p}\) be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution $X = A^+B$. (Here, ${}^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that \[ \|A \tilde X - B\|_{\rm F} \leq (1+\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)) \min_{X \in \mathbb R^{d \times p}}\|AX - B\|_{\rm F}? \]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $n,d,p,k$ be positive integers with $d\le n$. Call a (random) matrix $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $d$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$ if, for every fixed $d$-dimensional subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with orthonormal basis $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ the matrix $\Omega^{\top}U\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}$ has full column rank $d$ (equivalently, $\Omega$ is injective when restricted to $V$).

Problem. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be full column rank, let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, and let $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ be an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $d$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$. Define the sketch-and-solve approximation
$$\tilde X \;=\; (\Omega^{\top}A)^{+}(\Omega^{\top}B)\in\mathbb R^{d\times p},$$
where $M^{+}$ denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. Prove or disprove the following claim: it necessarily holds (with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$, or in expectation under any standard reading consistent with the injection guarantee) that
$$\|A\tilde X-B\|_{F}\;\le\;\bigl(1+\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\bigr)\,\min_{X\in\mathbb R^{d\times p}}\|AX-B\|_{F}.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_{F}$ is the Frobenius norm.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint titled "Oblivious Subspace Injection Is Not Enough for Relative Error" explicitly disproves the claim: it constructs counterexamples showing that the OSI property alone does not yield $(1+O(\varepsilon))$ relative-error guarantees for sketch-and-solve least squares (nor for randomized SVD in Frobenius norm). The bound is recoverable only under a strengthened injectivity on appropriate augmented subspaces.

status_evidence.title: Oblivious Subspace Injection Is Not Enough for Relative Error
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples show this for sketch-and-solve least squares and for randomized SVD in the Frobenius norm; OSI alone does not yield OSE-style relative-error guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: The relative-error sketch-and-solve guarantee under only an OSI assumption is disproved by explicit counterexamples.
